message:
Please review the following document.

Here is how its author describes it:

<author>
This bid is unusual in that it is not based on assumptions about demand: we tested the exact opening pattern at Ashgrove before asking for a penny, and measured the results hour by hour. The pilot showed strong uptake, with evening visits running close to daytime levels and Sunday sessions very popular with families, and new memberships up by about two-thirds on the year before. That gives Members real local evidence that the hours will be used. The costing is equally careful. Staffing is built up from first principles, hours times staff times weeks times branches at the correct graded rate with on-costs, and utilities are taken from actual pilot spend rather than estimates, all of which sums to £174,000. We also looked seriously at the cheaper self-service alternative and explain why it would cost more once building works are included. I am confident this is a well-tested, carefully costed proposal that delivers on the Council Plan.
</author>

<document>
Budget Justification: Extended Opening Hours at Five Branch Libraries, 2027-28
Library Services, Westmoor Borough Council, September 2026

1. Request
Library Services requests a growth bid of £174,000 in the 2027-28 revenue budget to extend opening hours at five branch libraries (Ashgrove, Fenwick, Holt Lane, Kingsmead and Millbrook) by ten hours a week each, from 38 to 48 hours.

2. Rationale
The five branches currently close at 5 pm on weekdays and do not open on Sundays. Residents' surveys have repeatedly identified opening hours as the main barrier to library use among working-age adults: in the 2025 Residents' Survey, 44% of non-users aged 25-54 said the library "is never open when I can go". The Council Plan commits to increasing library use among working-age residents and to supporting adult learning and job-seeking.

Each branch would add late opening until 8 pm on Tuesdays and Thursdays (six additional hours) and Sunday opening from 11 am to 3 pm (four additional hours).

3. Evidence from the Ashgrove pilot
From October 2025 to March 2026, Ashgrove trialled exactly this pattern, funded from one-off underspends.

Table 1. Ashgrove pilot: average visits per opening hour, October 2025 to March 2026
Time slot | Visits per hour
Weekday 9 am - 12 pm | 46
Weekday 12 pm - 5 pm | 58
Tuesday and Thursday 5 pm - 8 pm (new) | 21
Saturday 9 am - 1 pm | 64
Sunday 11 am - 3 pm (new) | 52

Over the pilot, Ashgrove recorded 1,140 new library memberships, compared with 690 in the same months a year earlier. Sunday sessions were particularly popular with families, and a weekly job club in the Thursday evening slot was fully booked from its third week.

Evening visits at Ashgrove averaged close to the weekday daytime level, which shows that there is strong latent demand for evening opening and that the new hours will be well used across all five branches.

4. Costs
Additional hours need two staff on duty at all times, in line with the Council's lone-working policy. Staffing is calculated on 50 weeks a year, allowing for bank holiday closures.

Table 2. Cost of extended hours, five branches
Item | Basis | Cost
Staffing | 10 hours x 2 staff x 50 weeks x 5 branches = 5,000 hours at £24.80 per hour (including on-costs) | £124,000
Utilities and caretaking | £6,500 per branch | £32,500
Self-service kiosk upgrades (maintenance contract) | 5 branches | £7,500
Total | | £174,000

The staffing rate is the mid-point of the Library Assistant grade plus 28% on-costs and an enhancement for Sunday working. Utilities and caretaking costs are based on the actual additional costs recorded at Ashgrove during the pilot, scaled to a full year.

5. Value for money
At current visit rates, the extra hours across the five branches would generate roughly 84,000 additional visits a year, at a cost of around £2 per visit. This compares favourably with the borough's average cost per library visit of £3.40.

6. Alternatives considered
We considered opening the branches with self-service access only in the extra hours, as some authorities have done. This would cut staffing costs by around two-thirds, but the Council's insurers have advised that unstaffed opening would require building alterations and CCTV at an estimated £60,000 per branch, and it would not support the job club and family activities that drove much of the pilot's success.

7. Risks
Recruitment. We expect to fill most additional hours from existing part-time staff who have asked for more hours, as happened during the pilot.
Demand at other branches. Ashgrove is our busiest branch, and demand at the other four may be lower. We will review usage after six months.

8. Conclusion
The twelve-month Ashgrove pilot has demonstrated strong demand for evening and Sunday opening, with new memberships up by two-thirds and evening use close to daytime levels. We ask Members to approve a growth bid of £174,000 to extend this successful model to all five branches from April 2027.
</document>
response:
The case for extended hours is plausible, and the Ashgrove pilot is useful local evidence. But the bid contains a **£10,000 arithmetic error in its own total**, and it misreads the pilot's central finding: evening visits ran at **less than half** the daytime rate, not "close to" it. It also gets the pilot's length wrong, and the visit projection assumes every branch will perform like the busiest one.

## What checks out

- **Staffing:** 10 × 2 × 50 × 5 = 5,000 hours, and at £24.80 an hour that is £124,000.
- **Utilities:** £6,500 × 5 = £32,500.
- **Memberships:** 1,140 against 690 is up 65%, about two-thirds as stated.
- **Visit projection arithmetic:** (6 evening hours × 21 + 4 Sunday hours × 52) × 50 weeks × 5 branches ≈ 84,000. The arithmetic is right, though the assumptions behind it aren't (see point 4).
- **Rationale:** the residents' survey finding (44% of non-users aged 25–54) is relevant and clearly presented.

## Major issues

**1. The total is £164,000, not £174,000.**
£124,000 + £32,500 + £7,500 = **£164,000**. Either a £10,000 line is missing from Table 2, or the bid asks for £10,000 more than its costing supports. Members will spot this, and it should be fixed before submission.

**2. Evening visits were well below daytime levels.**
Weekday daytime at Ashgrove averaged about **54 visits an hour** (46 in the morning, 58 in the afternoon, weighted by hours). The new evening slot averaged **21**, about 40% of the daytime rate. The bid's statement that evening visits "averaged close to the weekday daytime level," repeated in the conclusion, is not what Table 1 shows.

**Sunday** is the slot that matches daytime demand, at 52 visits an hour. This difference matters for value for money:

| New slot | Staff cost per hour (2 × £24.80) | Visits per hour (Ashgrove) | Staff cost per visit |
|---|---|---|---|
| Sunday | £49.60 | 52 | **≈ £0.95** |
| Tuesday/Thursday evening | £49.60 | 21 | **≈ £2.36** |

Evening hours cost about 2.5 times as much per visit as Sundays, at the busiest branch. That doesn't rule evenings out. The Thursday job club is a strong reason to keep at least one, and evenings serve working-age adults, the group the Council Plan targets. But it should be stated honestly, and it suggests an option the bid doesn't consider: Sunday opening plus **one** late evening.

**3. The pilot lasted six months, not twelve.**
Section 3 says October 2025 to March 2026, which is six months. The conclusion calls it a "twelve-month Ashgrove pilot."

**4. The visit projection assumes all five branches perform like Ashgrove.**
The risks section says Ashgrove is the busiest branch and the others may see lower demand. The 84,000 figure nonetheless applies Ashgrove's rates to all five. For illustration, if the other four reach 60% of Ashgrove's levels:
- visits fall to about **57,000**
- cost per visit rises to about **£2.90** (at £164,000), close to the borough average of £3.40

The projection should scale each branch by its current footfall relative to Ashgrove.

**Two related problems:**
- **Some visits in new hours may be displaced.** They may come from people who would otherwise have visited during existing hours, so the net increase in visits is smaller than the total in the new slots.
- **The cost comparison mixes two measures.** The £3.40 borough average includes fixed costs (buildings, stock, management). £2 is the extra cost of extra hours. They aren't directly comparable.

## Other points

- **The membership rise may not all be due to the new hours.** The figure covers all new members at Ashgrove, and publicity around the pilot may have contributed. Recording how many new members joined during the new slots would separate the effects.
- **Show how the £24.80 rate is built up.** The bid describes it as the grade mid-point plus 28% on-costs plus a Sunday enhancement, but gives no figures. Showing the calculation would let Finance check it, and would show how much Sunday working costs relative to evenings.
- **The utilities figure may be on the high side.** The pilot ran October to March, when heating and lighting costs are highest, so scaling it to a full year probably overstates the cost. That makes it a prudent figure, but say so. The other branches' buildings may also differ in size and running costs from Ashgrove's.
- **The kiosk maintenance contract** isn't explained. Why do extended hours require it?

## On the alternatives

Section 6 gives two reasons against self-service opening: the insurers' estimate for building works, and the loss of the job club and family activities. The second is a strong reason. The author's description goes further, saying self-service "would cost more once building works are included." That's only true in year one:

- **Self-service:** about £300,000 one-off (5 × £60,000), saving about £83,000 a year in staffing (two-thirds of £124,000). It breaks even in under four years.
- The building works would also come from the **capital** budget rather than revenue, a different decision for Members.

A fair comparison would show this over several years. It would also include a **mixed option**: staffed Sundays and job club evening, with self-service at other times.

## On the author's description

- **"Evening visits running close to daytime levels"** isn't accurate: 21 visits an hour against about 54. Sunday matches daytime demand; evenings don't.
- **"All of which sums to £174,000"** is wrong: the lines sum to £164,000.
- **"Staffing built up from first principles … at the correct graded rate"** is right for the hours calculation, but the rate itself isn't broken down.
- **"Self-service would cost more once building works are included"** holds in year one but not over several years.
- **The membership increase, the Sunday result and the job club** are accurately reported, and they are the strongest evidence in the bid.

## Suggested revisions

1. **Correct the total** to £164,000, or identify the missing £10,000 line.
2. **Describe the pilot accurately:** six months, strong Sunday demand, lower evening demand, and the job club as the main reason for evening opening.
3. **Project visits branch by branch,** scaled to each branch's current use, and estimate how many would be net additional.
4. **Add an option of Sunday plus one late evening,** costed against the full ten hours.
5. **Compare self-service over several years,** and include a mixed option.
6. **Show how the £24.80 rate is built up,** and explain the kiosk contract.

With these changes, the strongest case for Members is probably **Sunday opening across all branches plus a job-club evening**. That case rests on figures that hold up when checked.
